chunks: A group informed me, from Abū Muḥammad Hārūn ibn Mūsā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Saʿīd, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan; and Aḥmad ibn ʿAbdūn informed me, from ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Zubayr, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan, from Ayyūb ibn Nūḥ, from Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj, from Abī al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a woman in nifās who gives birth in the month of Ramadan after salat al-ʿaṣr: should she complete that day or break her fast? He said: “She should break her fast, then make up that day.”

Al-Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, said: The greatest number of days of nifās is eighteen days. So if the woman in nifās sees blood on the nineteenth day from her delivering the pregnancy, that is not from nifās; rather, it is istiḥāḍah. So she should act according to what we have outlined for the mustaḥāḍah, and she should pray and fast. Reports have also come, relied upon, stating that the furthest limit of nifās is ten days, and that is what I act upon because of their clarity in my view.

What is relied upon in this matter is that it has been established that the woman’s liability is bound by salat and fasting before her nifās without disagreement. So when nifās occurs to her, it is necessary that what had become binding upon her not fall away except by proof. There is no disagreement among the Muslims that when a woman sees the blood of nifās for ten days, and whatever exceeds that is disputed. So one should not move to that except by what conclusively removes excuse. Everything reported in the narrations that includes more than ten days consists of solitary reports that do not conclusively remove excuse, or a report that came out due to a specific circumstance or for taqiyyah, and I shall explain their meaning, if Allah the Exalted wills. This indicates what we have mentioned: that the furthest limit of the days of nifās is ten days.

key_terms.اسْتِحَاضَةٌ: irregular non-menstrual bleeding that does not suspend salat or fasting
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: the obligatory salat duties binding on the woman
key_terms.الصِّيَامِ: the obligatory fasting duties binding on the woman

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a woman who gives birth during the day in Ramadan, and what is the maximum length of nifās?
ai.summary: This hadith states that if a woman gives birth in Ramadan after salat al-ʿaṣr, she must break her fast and later make up that day. The accompanying legal discussion examines the maximum duration of nifās, mentioning eighteen days as one view while affirming reliance on reports indicating ten days as the strongest ruling, after which the blood is treated as istiḥāḍah and the woman resumes salat and fasting.
